spans.text: To test our hypotheses, a whole-brain statistical F -map was created of the RFX ANOVA F -test: picture type (low calorie food, high calorie food or neutral object) × attention focus (object/foods attended or bars attended).

The whole-brain analysis of the pictures (low calorie foods, high calorie foods vs. neutral objects) × attention focus (neutral object/food attended vs. bars attended), revealed a network of areas showing significant activity.
Selected participants were 12 right-handed, healthy students with a normal body weight

value: The whole-brain analysis revealed a network of areas showing significant activity, including the left amygdala and left medial OFC, and the attention manipulation strongly modulated activity in several regions. Explicit evaluation of foods was necessary for OFC activity, and activity in the amygdala was also dependent on attention focus.

definition.value: food (satiated) versus neutral (satiated) AND food (deprived) versus neutral (deprived), combined with the interaction between food deprivation and energy content

spans.text: Therefore, the conjunction test performed was food (satiated) versus neutral (satiated) AND food (deprived) versus neutral (deprived).
The whole-brain analysis of the effects of food deprivation in conjunction with the interaction with calorie revealed a network of significantly active areas
Selected participants were 12 right-handed, healthy students with a normal body weight

value: Conjunction effects analysis revealed no significant amygdala activation common to all food conditions versus neutral object conditions. However, attention-independent activity was found in the medial prefrontal cortex following presentation of high calorie foods, and the additional conjunction analysis showed hunger-by-calorie effects in the OFC, posterior cingulate cortex, insula, caudate putamen and fusiform gyrus.

spans.text: Conjunction effects analysis for brain activation common to all food conditions (both foods attended and bars attended conditions) versus the neutral object conditions (both objects attended and bars attended conditions) revealed no significant effect in the amygdala

description.value: Functional EPI volumes were input to Brainvoyager QX v1.9. The first two volumes of each run were discarded for magnetic saturation, followed by slice-timing correction, 3D rigid-body motion correction, high-pass filtering to remove low-frequency noise, and 6 mm FWHM isotropic Gaussian smoothing. Functional data were aligned with the averaged high-resolution anatomical scan and spatially normalized using Talairach transformation for group analysis.

spans.text: The first two volumes of the T2* weighted functional images were discarded due to magnetic saturation effects. Preprocessing comprised slice scan timing correction (using sinc interpolation), motion correction (using a 3D rigid-body transformation of each volume to the first volume of each run and using trilinear/sinc interpolation) and high-pass filtering to remove low-frequency noise (up to three cycles in the single run time-course). Individual functional data were smoothed using a 6 mm full-width-at-half-maximum isotropic Gaussian Kernel.

description.value: Participants attended to foods, neutral objects, or bars while viewing food and object pictures.

Participants viewed five high-calorie food pictures, each briefly presented with peripheral bars. Depending on the attention-focus block, they either evaluated and rated the food's palatability/taste by vividly imagining its taste, or attended to the bars and judged whether their orientations matched.

Participants viewed five low-calorie food pictures, each briefly presented with peripheral bars. Depending on the attention-focus block, they either evaluated and rated the food's palatability/taste by vividly imagining its taste, or attended to the bars and judged whether their orientations matched.

Participants viewed five neutral object pictures, each briefly presented with peripheral bars. In object-attended blocks they judged whether the object was red; in bars-attended blocks they judged whether the peripheral bar orientations matched.

spans.text: During the scanning session, the food, neutral object and bar-orientation conditions of the experimental task were presented in a blocked fashion.

instructions.value: Participants judged food palatability, object redness, or whether bars had similar orientations.
